summary: New Boston (Lewis County) Conservation Department tower of 1950, closed 1970 and removed 1982; loaned to Thompson Park Zoo in Watertown, restored in 2016 and open to the public there.

facts.design: 80-foot Aermotor LS40 tower, erected by the Conservation Department in 1950 at New Boston
facts.agency: Thompson Park Zoo, Watertown (current host); built by the NYS Conservation Department

access.note: On display on the Thompson Park Zoo grounds in Watertown; the chapter's list says it reopened to the public at the zoo in 2016; current climbing rules not confirmed

events.note: Erected by the Conservation Department as an 80-foot Aermotor LS40 at New Boston
Closed at the end of the 1970 season, with the advent of aerial detection
Dismantled and removed by DEC personnel to the Harrisville facilities
Moved into Thompson Park Zoo, Watertown, as a community education exhibit
Thompson Park Zoo restored the tower on its grounds; it stayed closed to the public until liability insurance could be secured
Grand opening at the zoo that summer; the tower is reported open to the public
FFLA $500 restoration grant for repairs; work completed that spring; the chapter's list says it reopened to the public at the zoo

notes_for_editor: Fact-check 2026-10-09: the towers6 entry for New Boston names no fires and no named observers, which is the basis for the story's statement that none were found. Build year conflict, unresolved: the NYSFFLA list gives 1950 for an 80-foot Aermotor LS40 at New Boston. A Waymarking listing that appeared only in search results says 1914 on Tug Hill; the page body could not be read, so it is not used. Reopening conflict, unresolved: the 2004 annual report says the tower was open after a 2004 grand opening, while the NYSFFLA list says it was restored and reopened in 2016; no source explains the gap. A 2016 Spectrum News item seen only as a search snippet calls the zoo tower the old Lowville tower; DEC and the chapter both say New Boston, so that snippet is treated as a mislabel and was not used. The record's 'moved 1999' is kept. The record's original New Boston entry (us-ny-new-boston) is Lewis County and matches DEC. Current climbing rules at the zoo were not found. Used 2 WebSearch and about 6 page reads plus cached local pages; the 2016 annual report was read earlier for another tower.
